title: Cycle Capacity Scenario Matrix and Staff Allocation Simulation
text:
Cycle Capacity Scenario Matrix and Staff Allocation Simulation

description:
Problem: Mid-cycle decommits and repeated scope shuffles are costing engineering ~10-15% of delivery velocity and creating churn on cross-team initiatives. We lack a repeatable quantitative runbook that ties staff availability, skill overlap, and contingency buffers to a recommended tranche/trim plan.

Goal: Produce a practical playbook and a lightweight simulation tool (Monte Carlo-backed spreadsheet + quick script) that both PMs and Eng leads can use during planning to: 1) enumerate plausible capacity scenarios, 2) recommend where to place soft-freeze buffers vs. hard commitments, 3) suggest role-level shadowing and surge lanes, and 4) propose scoped cuts that minimize customer-facing risk.

Success metrics: reduce mid-cycle decommit rate from ~18% to <8% across pilot initiatives; increase accuracy of committed scope (features delivered vs committed) from 72% to 85% for participating teams; time-to-decision in planning reduced to under 90 minutes for medium-sized initiatives.

Approach:
- Design a scenario matrix capturing: staffing uncertainty bands, skill pool overlap, dependency criticality, and external risk multipliers (sales commitments, infra incidents).
- Implement a Monte Carlo simulation prototype (Python notebook + Google Sheet wrapper) to produce distributions of completion probability per initiative given different buffer allocations.
- Convert outputs into a decision matrix: for each initiative, recommended commit tier (Guaranteed / Contingent / Deferred), suggested staff shadowing % and minimum surge lanes.
- Author a 1-page playbook summarizing steps, roles, and templates for PM/Eng leads to run during pre-cycle planning.

Deliverables: scenario matrix template (GSheet), simulation notebook (Colab link), playbook PDF in Confluence, trimmed-scope decision checklist, Slackbot workflow to record final tranche choices into the planning board.

Risks: simulation relies on historical velocity distributions which may be sparse for newly-formed teams; cultural resistance to enforced surge lanes; potential misinterpretation of outputs as prescriptive rather than advisory. Mitigations: conservative priors, running two sensitivity passes (optimistic/pessimistic), include human review gate in the process.

acceptance_criteria:
Simulation tool produces probability distributions for initiative delivery under at least 3 buffer configurations.
Playbook and templates published to Confluence with an example run for a cross-team initiative.
Product and Eng leads complete a pilot planning session using the tool and provide structured feedback.
Dashboards updated to track mid-cycle decommit rates for pilot initiatives.

comments:
2026-02-16 — Ava McKenzie: Started baseline data export from Jira velocity and historical decommit logs. Noticed high variance for teams with <3 historical cycles; added conservative prior for those teams.
2026-02-22 — Owen Park: Eng architecture counterpoint — we need to include infra risk multiplier from the runtime team (ENG-2245) before finalizing recommendations; asked infra to provide incident frequency by quarter.
2026-02-28 — Priya Verma (engineering lead): Reviewed initial simulation; suggested adding role-level constraints (e.g., single-owner tasks) and a 'shadowing cost' estimate to avoid undercounting coordination overhead.
2026-03-03 — Design review (Slack): UX templates for the playbook approved; requested a one-page 'read-me' for exec summary that can be pasted into stakeholder updates.
2026-03-08 — Owen Park: Ran a pilot with Data Platform and Console teams (two initiatives). Results: recommended reducing commit by 1 tranche for Initiative A, keeping Initiative B with contingency buffer. Logged pilot notes in Confluence and opened follow-ups for fine-tuning thresholds.
2026-03-11 — PM review session: Product leadership asked for tie-in to OKR scoring (impact x confidence) — added a new column in the matrix to capture OKR alignment and to bias hard-commit recommendations when OKR impact is very high.
2026-03-12 — Ava McKenzie: Submitted draft playbook and link to simulation notebook for review (see attachments). Requesting approvals and scheduling a training drop-in on 2026-03-18.

follow_up_tasks:
Finalize priors for teams with sparse history and document methodology
Integrate infra incident multiplier from ENG-2245 into the notebook
Add OKR alignment column and recalc recommendation thresholds
Publish playbook and run two 30-minute training sessions with PMs/Eng leads
Instrument Grafana dashboard to capture pilot metrics and make them visible in planning docs

notes:
Avoid using simulation outputs as absolute mandates. The playbook will emphasize a 'human in the loop' checklist: validate high-impact recommendations with exec sponsor and Eng lead before freezing scope.
